title: attention-sparsity-triggered-kernel-switchover-playbook-may2025
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for diagnosing, reproducing, and mitigating cases where attention sparsity patterns in client prompts (or model-internal masks) cause the serving runtime to switch kernels unexpectedly, leading to throughput drops, tail-latency spikes, or subtle quality regressions when running AWQ / GPTQ quantized variants (INT8/FP8).

Context / motivation:
- Over the last two weeks we saw three customer incidents where p95/p99 latency jumped by 2–4x on AWQ-int8 bundles for long-form generation workloads.
- Initial traces show that the serving runtime dispatches an "alternate attention kernel" for certain sparsity patterns (high fraction of zeroed attention rows, long padding prefixes, or chunked attention masks coming from tokenizers).
- The alternate kernel is correct functionally but paths into it are not as well-optimized (suboptimal vectorization and cache layout), and sometimes it uses a fallback FP32 path for a tiny subset of ops.

High-level hypothesis:
1) Sparse attention patterns cross a heuristic threshold in kernel selector that flips to a more conservative kernel (safety-first) which is slower on GPU due to reduced lane utilization.
2) For quantized weights (AWQ/GPTQ) the slower kernel triggers additional dequant/ requant ops or more frequent KV cache materialization, amplifying cost and affecting tail latencies.
3) Small changes in prompt prefix length or mask representation can flip the dispatch, so customer behavior is non-deterministic and brittle.

Quick reproduction recipe (minimal):
- Model: trimmed GPT-style 2.7B (open-model-testbed) with AWQ-int8 weights (our internal bundle).
- Hardware: single A100-40GB and one H100-80GB for cross-arch checks.
- Client harness: 64 concurrent streams, arrival process: Poisson lambda tuned to keep 80% p50 saturation.
- Two prompt templates:
  * Dense prompt: natural text 512 tokens, attention mask all ones.
  * Sparse prompt: same text but insert 200-token padding block near token 128 (mask zeros for those positions) + add chunked mask from tokenizer (simulate streaming chunking).
- Run both templates for 30 minutes each, sample p50/p95/p99, kernel dispatch logs, GPU utilization, and nvprof traces every 5 minutes.

Observed metrics (representative runs):
- Dense prompt (A100, AWQ-int8): throughput 430 tokens/s, p95 = 210 ms, p99 = 310 ms, GPU util 78%
- Sparse prompt (A100, AWQ-int8): throughput 130 tokens/s, p95 = 780 ms, p99 = 1200 ms, GPU util 35%
- Trace artifact: kernel_selector logged "attention_kernel_v2_fallback" on 98% of sparse prompt requests; dense used "attention_kernel_v1_vec".
- Micro-analysis: v2_fallback spends 42% of time in a non-vectorized loop doing per-token mask checks and a path that touches FP32 accumulators for a pooling op.

Cross-check: GPTQ and FP8 variants
- GPTQ-int8: similar dispatch pattern, but throughput drop smaller (~2.5x) because GPTQ kernels have a slightly different mask merge step (we still see p99 inflation).
- FP8: generally uses a different kernel family and avoids the fallback for same masks, so FP8 runs had only ~1.2x slowdown for sparse prompts but with slightly higher median latency compared to AWQ-dense.

Root causes identified so far:
- Kernel selector heuristic: uses a sparsity_ratio threshold computed on masked rows (if > 0.18 then pick fallback). This threshold was tuned in 2024 for CPU-side correctness on some models, never stress-tested at scale on GPU quantized stacks.
- Fallback kernel: implemented originally to ensure numeric stability with irregular masks; it has rarely used code paths and lacks kernel-level optimizations for current GPU architectures (uncoalesced loads, scalar branches).
- Quantization interactions: AWQ dequant path gets invoked inside the fallback because we currently only have an in-register fused dequant for kernel_v1; kernel_v2 calls a generic dequant helper that forces memory traffic.

Immediate mitigations (short-term):
- Patch kernel selector to use a higher sparsity threshold for GPU backends (experimental toggle): sparsity_threshold_gpu = 0.35.
- Inline a light-weight path inside kernel_v2 that mirrors the register-fused dequant used by v1 for AWQ/GPTQ bundles (fast-path flag AWQ_FUSED_DEQUANT=true).
- Add runtime telemetry: expose kernel dispatch reason code in per-request traces so we can map customer prompts to kernel decisions.

Validation plan for mitigations:
- A/B rollout on dedicated staging cluster: 10% traffic -> 50% -> 100% over 48 hours, monitor p50/p95/p99, error rates, and output quality checks (BLEU/ROUGE/likelihood on a fixed prompt set).
- Regression targets: no more than 5% accuracy delta vs baseline dense-run outputs; tail-latency p95 should not exceed baseline by more than 20%.

Longer-term playbook changes (under engineering backlog):
- Kernel selector refactor to be model- and backend-aware (not just mask ratio). Input features to selector should include: sequence length distribution, mask entropy, KV-cache locality, quantization scheme, and backend (A100/H100).
- Implement a lightweight mask-normalization pass at tokenizer/embedding stage that canonicalizes chunked masks into a compact representation to reduce accidental sparsity triggers. This would be configurable per-customer.
- Add microbench suite: synthetic generator that produces controlled sparsity patterns (clustered zeros, interleaved zeros, streaming-chunk masks) so kernels are exercised deterministically in CI.
notes: TO-DO: run H100 microprofiling with l2/cache counters; create small repro case for FP32-accumulator divergence; sync with solutions-eng on customers that reported incidents; add test vector to nightly smoke tests. Questions: should we prefer widening kernels to handle sparsity or normalize masks upstream?
